item.title: Renting an Apartment in Germany: What Apartment Hunting in Munich Is Really Like
item.description:
Renting an apartment in Germany is genuinely a stressful process. Especially in Munich and the surrounding area, prices are very high and the number of applicants is huge. In this post, as someone who recently moved here, I share what I experienced and learned step by step.

Everything starts with an address: Anmeldung
#

For someone newly moving to Germany, the first task is finding a place to live. Because once you find an apartment, you go to the local registration office (Bürgeramt) and register your address with an Anmeldung (address registration), declaring “I live at this address.” For this, you need a document from the landlord (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung); you are expected to register within 2 weeks of moving in.

item.title: Istanbul to Munich by Car: Via Romania in 2 Days with Kids
item.description:
When we moved to Germany, we decided to drive our own car instead of flying. We had a lot of luggage, and a connecting flight with two small children (then aged 1 and 5) did not appeal to us. We drove more than 2,000 km from Istanbul to Munich through Bulgaria, Romania, Hungary and Austria in two days. Here is our route and what helped us on the way.

Our route
#

  1. Istanbul → Kapıkule: the exit from Turkey. As it is an EU external border, passport and vehicle checks happen here.
  2. Bulgaria: Sofia → Vidin: after Sofia there is a mountainous road north-west towards the Romanian border. We drove it at night; it was narrow, winding and foggy in places, the most tiring part of the trip. Drive it in daylight if you can.
  3. Vidin–Calafat bridge into Romania: the bridge has a toll. In Romania we took the A1 motorway towards the Hungarian border (Arad / Nădlac).
  4. Hungary: one night in Budapest: we stopped halfway in Budapest; we paid €80 for the night back then. Sleeping in a real bed made the second day much easier.
  5. Austria: Vienna → Linz → Passau: on the last day we drove via Vienna and Linz and entered Germany at Passau.

Why Romania and not Serbia?
#

The Serbian route looks shorter on the map. But we bought our green card insurance at the Bulgarian border as a cheap EU-only policy, and Serbia is not in the EU. So we kept the whole route inside the EU. I explain how in our green card insurance post.

item.title: Driving an LPG Car from Turkey to Germany: Don't Leave Without an Adapter
item.description:
When we moved from Turkey to Germany, we drove our 2020 Honda Civic, which runs on LPG. The plan was simple: drive the whole way on cheap LPG. That worked perfectly through Bulgaria and Romania. Then we reached Budapest, and our LPG journey ended there.

This post explains what happened and what anyone driving an LPG car from Turkey to Europe should know before setting off.

The problem: LPG nozzles are not the same everywhere
#

Most LPG cars in Turkey have a DISH filler connector. Pumps in Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania fit it. But Europe does not use a single standard. In Germany and Austria the common type is ACME, and some countries use Bayonet.

item.title: Your Child's Passport to the World: Essential Travel Documents from Germany
item.description: As Turkish families and expats living in Germany, we often find ourselves navigating a beautiful blend of cultures and, of course, a good deal of German bureaucracy. While we love the freedom of travel that comes with living in the heart of Europe, one area that consistently causes stress for us, especially when traveling with children, is the mountain of documents required. I’ve heard countless stories, and experienced a few myself, of families being delayed or even denied boarding because of missing paperwork for their little ones. It’s a situation no one wants to be in, particularly after months of planning that perfect family vacation!

item.title: Fired in Germany: Termination by Email, Labour Court and Settlement
item.description:
Being fired in Germany was both a shock and a bureaucratic marathon for me: a termination by email, the labour court, the Jobcenter and a settlement. Here is what happened and what I wish I had known earlier.

Note: This is not legal advice, just my own experience. For your own case, talk to a lawyer or the advice desk at the labour court.

The termination came by email, and that is not valid
#

I found out I was being let go by email. In Germany a termination (Kündigung) must be in writing, on paper, with a handwritten signature. Email, fax or a scanned document is not a legally valid termination.

item.title: Germany Job Seeker Visa: I Waited a Year for an Appointment (It Is Now the Opportunity Card)
item.description:
Before I moved to Germany, I applied for the German job seeker visa. The invitation for the visa appointment arrived about a year later. By then my Bulgarian citizenship had come through, so as an EU citizen I no longer needed a visa and never continued the application.

So I can’t tell you how the job seeker visa ends. What I can tell you is what the waiting taught me, and how the system works today, because the visa I applied for no longer exists.
